items.title: 68113_Barney Bigard oral history interview
items.q: The interviewee (Barney Bigard) narrates stories about Louis Armstrong and his wife Lucille, but does not describe a direct personal interaction or relationship with Lucille herself.

ctx.x: Louis was a wonderful man to work with. I mean, he'd say a lot of things. He can raise hell with you. Now in two seconds he'd forgotten all about it and forgot even what it was all about.

I kidded him. One time, for no reason whatsoever -- we were at the Blue Note in Chicago -- and, well, if he had a fuss with his wife, Lucille, and he came off the stand. He said, 'Cats think because they played in a big band that they are the best musicians in town, the greatest band. They think they're hell and everyone thinks because he was with Paul Whiteman, he thinks he's hell, too.' So I'm listening. I said, 'What is all this about?'

And I hadn't even said one word to him. Neither has Jack. Nobody. And he's mumbling all this in his dressing room. So I said, "Well, I know you must be hinting at me, but if you are, I'm sure glad I was with the greatest band in the world, because your band wasn't nothing." I said, "You had the world's worst band." And he kept griping.
